title: jpipe-runner report 2.1
description: What a run of jpipe-runner concluded (ADR-0011): every element of the justification, with its status, its step and what that step declares, observed and produced; then every diagnostic. Within a major version, a minor version only adds optional fields: a consumer ignores fields it does not know. This schema is strict, so that the runner cannot emit a field it does not document. Documented in docs/report-schema.md.

justification.description: The justification's name, or null if the model was refused before it could be read.

verdict.description: fail if an element failed; skip if none failed and one was skipped; pass if every element passed; invalid if nothing ran, because the model was refused, a step library could not be imported, or validation reported an error; valid if the run was a dry run and validation reported no error, so that no step was called.

strict.description: Whether the run was strict: validation counted warnings as errors, and the command line failed a skipped verdict.

elements.description: Every element of the justification, in the order the runner takes them: each after the elements that support it. Empty if the model was refused.

diagnostics.description: Every problem found: loading the model, importing the libraries or validating them, then running each element, in topological order.

diagram.description: The path of the diagram drawn for this run, its dataflow, relative to the directory the runner ran in when it is under it, or null.

selection.description: What an incremental run (--incremental) ran again, or null for a full run (ADR-0039). New in 2.1.

baseline.description: The report the run compared with, as the command line gave it.

rerun.description: Each element that ran again, by id, in topological order, and why. Every other element was reused.

summary.description: How many elements ended in each status, and how many diagnostics of each severity. pass + fail + skip + not_run = elements.

aliases.description: The ids of the elements that composition merged into this one.

supports.description: The ids of the elements it supports.

reason.description: Why it did not pass: the reason its step gave, the problem found, or the elements that stopped it.

blocked_by.description: The elements upstream that stopped it, failed or skipped on their own account. Empty unless it was skipped because of them.

ran.description: Whether its step was called; for an element reused, in the run that decided it.

reused.description: Whether an incremental run took it from its baseline, as decided there, rather than run it again (ADR-0039). New in 2.1.

bound_to.description: The step bound to it, as module.function, or null if it is unbound.

bound_by.description: The ids, as the step names them, that designate this element.

library_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file that declares its step, or null if it is unbound or its step has no file: what tells an incremental run that the step's code changed (ADR-0039). New in 2.1.

observes.description: The files, as globs relative to where the runner runs, that what its step observes depends on: a change to one of them reaches the element. A wildcard in the name of a directory the runner put in front of a path is escaped, as in checks[[]v2]/*.md.

sources.description: Everything its step declares it observes, as each describes itself: a path or a glob relative to where the runner runs, a file and a JSON Pointer (package.json#/version), an environment variable (env:CI), or what an observable of the step library answers. A path is escaped as in observes. Since 2.0.

consumes.description: The variables its step declares it consumes, each once.

inputs.description: What each parameter of its step receives, by parameter: the variable, and the id of the element whose step produced it, among the element's supporters, or null if it resolves to no single one (ADR-0031). Since 2.0.

produces.description: The variables its step declares it produces.

produced.description: The values its step produced, by variable.

artifacts.description: The files its step observed, recorded just before it was called.

observations.description: What its step observed that is not a file, recorded just before it was called. Since 2.0.

value.description: A produced value: the value itself if it is JSON, otherwise its Python repr and type.

artifact.description: A file an evidence observed. A glob that matched nothing is recorded once, under its pattern, as unreachable.

path.description: Relative to where the runner runs, with / as separator.

declared.description: The one of the element's sources that designates it. Since 2.0.

value.description: The value observed in the file, when what was observed is a value in it. Since 2.0.

reachable.description: Whether what was observed could be reached: the file read and, for a value in it, the value found.

read.description: The file as the run read it, when it is unreachable all the same: what was observed in it was not found, such as the value a JSON Pointer designates. Since 2.0.

observation.description: Something an evidence observed that is not a file, such as an environment variable.

declared.description: The one of the element's sources that designates it.

variable.description: The environment variable it is the value of, or null if it is not one. jpipe-runner status reads it again; anything else that is not a file needs a new run.

hidden.description: Whether what was observed is kept out of the report: neither its value nor its SHA-256 is recorded, and only a new run can tell whether it changed.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the value written as JSON, or null if it could not be reached or is hidden.

value.description: The value observed, or null if it could not be reached or is hidden.

code.description: The contract: a code never changes meaning. docs/rules.md lists them.

element.description: The id of the element it is about, if it is about one.

message.description: Written for people: it may be reworded in any release.

traceback.description: The exception behind it, for a step that raised (JP022) or a library that failed to import (JP020).

exception.description: The exception's type, qualified by its module unless it is a built-in.

frames.description: The frames of the step's or library's own code, from the outermost call to where it was raised.

cause.description: The exception it was raised from, or while handling.

file.description: Relative to where the runner runs, with / as separator, when the file is under it.
